question: A 63-year-old woman, gravida 0, para 0 comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of abdominal distension, constipation, and weight loss. She has a history of endometriosis. Pelvic examination shows a nontender, irregular, left adnexal mass. Her serum level of CA-125 is elevated. Serum concentrations of human chorionic gonadotropin and alpha-fetoprotein are within the reference ranges. Microscopic examination of the mass is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Large undifferentiated germ cells with clear cytoplasm
options.opb: Flattened, cuboidal cells along with Schiller-Duval bodies
options.opc: Small, round cells that form Call-Exner bodies
options.opd: Atypical epithelial cells along with psammoma bodies
options.ope: Spindle-shaped stromal cells along with signet ring cells

analysis: The clinical presentation of a postmenopausal woman with abdominal distension, constipation, weight loss, and an elevated CA-125 level along with a left adnexal mass raises suspicion for ovarian cancer. The presence of Call-Exner bodies is characteristic of granulosa cell tumors, which are a type of sex cord-stromal tumor. These tumors are associated with estrogen production and can present with abdominal distension and elevated CA-125 levels.
